content: The following are detailed descriptions of the various formulations and packaging of clarithromycin, marketed under the brand name Biaxin® by AbbVie Inc.: 1. Biaxin® Filmtab® Tablets (250 mg and 500 mg) These are film-coated tablets containing clarithromycin, USP, available in two strengths: 250 mg and 500 mg. The 250 mg tablets are packaged as 60 tablets per container, with the National Drug Code (NDC) 0074-2586-60. The 500 mg tablets are also packaged as 60 tablets per container, with the NDC 0074-3165-60. Both formulations are prescription-only (Rx only) and manufactured by AbbVie Inc. 2. Biaxin® XL Filmtab® Extended-Release Tablets (500 mg) These are extended-release tablets containing clarithromycin, USP, at a strength of 500 mg. They are available in multiple packaging options: A 60-tablet container with NDC 0074-2586-11. A 100-tablet container labeled specifically for households without young children, with NDC 0074-3165-41. Additionally, a 14-tablet unit-of-use package is available, designed for a 7-day course of treatment. This package includes instructions for taking two tablets once daily with food. The NDC for this unit-of-use package is 0074-3165-11. These formulations are also prescription-only (Rx only). 3. Biaxin® Granules for Oral Suspension (125 mg/5 mL and 250 mg/5 mL) This formulation is a granulated powder that, when mixed, forms an oral suspension of clarithromycin, USP. It is available in two concentrations: 125 mg per 5 mL, with a total volume of 100 mL when reconstituted. The NDC for this formulation is 0074-3188-13. 250 mg per 5 mL, also with a total volume of 100 mL when reconstituted. The NDC for this formulation is 0074-3188-13. Both concentrations are prescription-only (Rx only). 4. Manufacturing Information The Biaxin® Filmtab® tablets and Biaxin® XL extended-release tablets are manufactured by AbbVie Ltd. in Barceloneta, Puerto Rico (PR 00617). The Biaxin® granules for oral suspension are manufactured by AbbVie Inc. in North Chicago, Illinois (IL 60064). 5. The unit-of-use packaging for Biaxin® XL includes a clear warning not to accept the product if the blister seal is broken. All formulations are clearly labeled as prescription-only (Rx only) and are intended for use under the guidance of a healthcare professional.
